text.p: ** BIRTHDAYS **
American painter, JAMES MCNEILL WHISTLER, who was best known for his "Portrait of My Mother", was born in 1834.
French novelist, MARCEL PROUST, whose masterpiece was 'Remembrance of Things Past', was born in 1871.
Australian cricketer, KEITH STACKPOLE, was born in 1940.
American singer, ARLO GUTHRIE, whose biggest hit was the album 'Alice's Restaurant', was born in 1947.

British singer and songwriter with the 'Pet Shop Boys', NEIL TENNANT, was born in 1954. Hits have included "West End Girls" (1985), "It's A Sin" (1987), "Always On My Mind" (1987), and "It's Alright" (1989).
Canadian guitarist and songwriter, DERRY GREHAN, from 'Honeymoon Suite', was born in 1957.
** EVENTS **
138 : Roman emperor, HADRIAN, who sponsored the building
of Hadrian's wall across northern Britain to keep the Scots out of England, died.
1099 : The famed Spanish warrior hero EL CID (RODRIGO
DIAZ de VIVAR), died, apparently from grief after his forces were defeated by the Moors.
1460 : In the Wars of the Roses, RICHARD of York defeated
King HENRY VI at the battle of Northampton.
1553 : Lady JANE GREY was proclaimed Queen of England
after the death of EDWARD VI; she ruled for only 10 days before being imprisoned and replaced by MARY I.
1754 : The representative for Pennsylvania, BENJAMIN
FRANKLIN, presented a proposal for unification of the British colonies in North America.
1858 : Australia's first fatal train crash occurred in
the Sydney suburb of Lidcombe. A train travelling from Campbelltown left the tracks on a sharp curve and several carriages overturned, killing four people and injuring 13 others.
1938 : American multi-millionaire, HOWARD HUGHES, set off

from New York on an around-the-world flight. HUGHES set a new record, taking just three days, 19 hours and 17 minutes. He and his four-man crew cut in half the previous around-the-world record set five years earlier.
1940 : The Luftwaffe attacked a British convoy in the
English Channel.
1940 : In World War Two, the Battle of Britain began when
at least 70 German bombers attacked docks in south Wales.
1941 : American ragtime piano player, JELLY ROLL MORTON,
died in Los Angeles.
1943 : U.S. 7th and British 8th armies began the invasion
of Sicily.
1962 : Telstar, the first television telecommunications
satellite was launched from Cape Canaveral, making possible the first relaying of television programmes across the Atlantic.
1964 : The Bahamas gained their independence from
Britain.
1975 : American singer, CHER, filed for divorce after
only ten days of marriage to GREG ALLMAN.
1985 : The Greenpeace protest ship Rainbow Warrior sank

in Auckland Harbour after two explosions tore the hull apart. A Greenpeace photographer was killed, but nine others on board escaped injury. The vessel was preparing to lead a protest flotilla into the French nuclear testing site at Muroroa Atoll in the Pacific. Two French government agents were sentenced to ten years jail for their part in the bombing. ALAIN MAFART and DOMINIQUE PRIEUR served three years of their sentence on the
French Polynesian island of Hao.
1991 : BORIS YELTSIN sworn in as the first elected
President of Russia that also saw the symbolic burial of Communist power in the vast republic.
1992 : Former Panamanian dictator MANUEL NORIEGA was
sentenced to 40 years in jail in the United States for allowing his country to be used for drug smuggling.
